A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DenseVLM research, despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and sufficiently complete for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DenseVLM benchmark results, ablations, SA-1B scaling experiments, and downstream detection and segmentation results, including supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original DenseVLM experiments and adds results for generated category sets, retrieval-model capacity, and additional competing methods.

M1.justification: v2 adds an optional category-construction route using NXTP-generated categories and DeepSeek-R1 foreground/background grouping. The written per-image objective changes from summing retained-region losses to averaging them. The core region extraction, retrieval, denoising, and decoupled KL alignment remain intact; the PDFs do not establish whether the normalization change reflects revised implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COCO, ADE20K, SA-1B, PASCAL Context, OV-COCO, and OV-LVIS coverage. Generated vocabularies and different retrieval-model sizes are tested within retained tasks and data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds FineCLIP to the dense-representation comparison and adds CAT-Seg+CLIPSelf, CAT-Seg+FineCLIP, F-ViT+CLIPSelf, and F-ViT+FineCLIP to Tables 7–8. These substantially expand direct comparisons with closely related alignment methods across segmentation and both detection benchmarks. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New ablations evaluate generated vocabularies containing 210 and 794 categories and compare ViT-B/16 with ViT-L/14 as DenseVLM retrieval models. The established splits, evaluation metrics, image resolutions, and training budgets otherwise remain unchanged. The reversed asterisk convention in backbone tables preserves the underlying initialization assignments.

E4.justification: v2 extends validation of central assumptions through generated-versus-annotated vocabulary experiments and a retrieval-model capacity ablation (Tables 4–5). It adds category-wise mask accuracy analysis (Figure 4) and revises foreground-bias examples and similarity maps. The threshold study is relocated to Appendix C with unchanged results; supplementary confusion matrices and patch examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, standard deviations, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Both present point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial comparator, vocabulary-source, retrieval-model, and category-wise results. Its main DenseVLM row substitutes values matching the existing 273-category ablation for the earlier 316-category values, including COCO box accuracy changing from 73.4 to 72.3; this does not establish same-setting deterioration. Table 7 changes CAT-Seg+DenseVLM A-847 mIoU from 12.1 to 12.2 and corrects its A-150 gain from 2.1 to 2.7. Two decoupling-ablation Mask-T entries also change by 0.1.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the separate expected negative-log-likelihood expression and revises the loss definition following Equation (5) from a sum to a mean over retained regions. The other mathematical definitions and KL branches remain equivalent after notation changes. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the introduction's category-guidance claim to include generative-model predictions; v1 describes dataset-derived category sets. The principal claims of reducing foreground bias, improving downstream dense prediction, and scaling with unlabeled images are retained.

C2.justification: v2 discusses category-set annotation dependence and presents generation as a way to address it. It interprets gains with a smaller retrieval model as evidence of reduced foreground bias and newly attributes foreground-bias problems to logits distillation. Appendix A's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-access link and identifies NXTP and DeepSeek-R1 for category generation and grouping. It clarifies ground-truth-based region evaluation and corrects the framework table's per-card memory notation from 4*37G/4*39G to 37G/39G. Conversely, Table 7 removes backbone identifiers. The detailed training configuration is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to FineCLIP, SILC, perceptual grouping, CLIP-DINOiser, NXTP, and DeepSeek-R1. It removes DIME-FM, CLIP-KD, and the feature-distillation citation together with their associated comparison paragraph. These update nearby research positioning while retaining the paper's focus on region-language alignment and foreground bias.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, renames L-VLM to U-VLM, and rewrites selected introductory, methodological, and experimental passages. The comparison and ablation subsections exchange order, and the threshold study moves to Appendix C. The overall narrative and section framework remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 1's example, redraws the framework diagram, adds the category-accuracy chart, revises similarity-map examples, and moves scaling-plot legends. It adds the retrieval-model table, expands category and downstream comparison tables, removes Table 7's backbone column, and relocates several displays. Appendix confusion matrices and patch illustrations are merely renumbered.

improvement.justification: The additional downstream controls and tests of vocabulary construction and retrieval-model dependence make the empirical support more informative, while the code link improves access information. Reporting problems limit the benefit: Section 4.2 retains 4.3/3.9-point mask gains although revised Table 1 implies 3.4/3.2, and Figure 3 marks the text encoder as trainable despite the implementation section stating that only the image encoder is trained. The added evidence supports a modest net improvement despite these inconsistencies.
